svg.title: How Rapport runs on Kubernetes
svg.desc: Animated architecture diagram, looping through one encounter that starts when Bo taps Accept. One web page (Ava's phone, the swarm panel and Bo's phone) talks to the gateway over REST and Server-Sent Events. In namespace team-rapport, the FastAPI gateway serves the public port 8080 and the cluster-only port 8081, and creates an Encounter with a traceparent for the kopf operator. The operator starts a delegate Job in org-acme (initiator) and a delegate Job plus Service in org-bluefin (responder). The delegates exchange three rounds of rapport.exchange/v1, each checking every outbound item with its own company's OPA, and report events to the gateway with POST /internal/events on port 8081. The gateway calls each company's private briefer. Briefers and delegates read Elasticsearch with scoped keys: briefers read their company's internal and shareable indices plus rapport-conference; delegates read only their shareable index and rapport-conference. Every Rapport pod exports OTLP to Dash0 (OPA does not), Radar Cloud watches the cluster, and a push to GitHub main runs an Action that builds the image into GHCR and commits its tag to deploy/; Argo CD, running in the vcluster, syncs deploy/ from main, and the pods pull the image from GHCR.
svg.text: One encounter, looping: Bo taps Accept, an Encounter starts two short-lived delegate pods, 3 policy-checked rounds run, and events reach every screen.
